a spring gushed forth from the tears of Manto at Claros. And Rhacius was so named because of his poverty and wretched clothing. 〈He is also called Lacius;〉 for λ is akin to ρ, as in ὑδρηλοί for ὑδρηροί.
2 supplied by Bethe | 3 τὸ λ̄ τῷ ρ̄ in L : τῷ λ̄ τὸ ρ̄ in F : differently in P
311-12a. 〈κεκλομένων:〉 all together being summoned and shouting approval. Lm
b. τῷ δὲ ξύμβλητο: this was a sign for overcoming the contest, both that she was older and that she was a priestess.
c. ξύμβλητο: she met. Lg (P)
d. πολιηόχου: of the one who guards cities. L
f. ἀρήτειρα: priestess.
313-14a. καί μιν δεξιτερῆς: it is also written thus 〈χειρὸς κύρεν〉, so that it means: and he touched her right hand. L

6 l. τῷ δὲ ξ. in P : χειρὸς κύρεν in L | 7 ἡ Ἰφιὰς added before καὶ ὅτι in P | 9 scholia 311/12d, 311/12f, 313/14a are in the lower margin in L | 10 πολιήοχος W : -ιοῦχος | 11 P adds ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀρητήρ, ὥσπερ ἀπὸ τοῦ σ[α]ωτὴρ σώτειρα | 12 γράφεται W : ἔδει L : ἔκειτο proposed by K | the variant reading preserved in the false lemma of scholium 311/12 b should be inserted here, as K saw
b. οὐδέ τι φάσθαι: the καί must be understood; nevertheless, though eager to speak, she did not succeed. For ἔμπης here means 'nevertheless'. L
14 τὸν in HF : τὸ in L
319. 〈δειδέχατ’:〉 they welcomed or received. Lg
320. προμολῆς: with the advances. Or it is written προμολὼν instead of προελθὼν, 'having come forward, he stood by'. L

322. καταβλώσκοντας: going down, coming down. β is used for μ; for β and π are akin to μ. Hence also a morsel is called βλωμός from βλώσκειν through the throat, that is, to go down, and Homer calls a pine βλωθρήν, the one that goes up to the aether.
19 κατερχομένους Lg | 20 τῷ in K : τῷ in L : differently in P
323. 〈παρὲκ νόον:〉 contrary to expectation. Lg
324. δέρμα δ’ ὁ μέν: it was customary for heroes to wear skins. Lm(P)
325. 〈αὐτὰρ ὅ:〉 Acastus. Lg
354. 〈παρασχεδόν:〉 immediately. Lg
389. 〈ἀιδνή:〉 dark. Sm
401a. ἐυστείρης: with a good keel. And οἰήια are the rudders, as it were οἰήσια, because the helmsman has need of steering (οἴησις). But the glossographers say τοὺς οἴακας.
